entry_state: Chapter 1 establishes that identical historical journals can hide different rate exposures; the first demonstration must preserve alternative company histories, information revisions and conditional statements with traceable assumptions. Forecast accuracy and full sector execution require later evidence. The next chapter must make this concrete for a complete company and a public disclosure.
exit_state: Northstar now supplies a complete scoped annual/interim history, a correction, joint scenario statements and consistent state/receipt semantics. Its forecast is explicitly archival conditional work rather than information available in January. A second parent/subsidiary company opens the problem of shared cash, intragroup margin and tax across accounting methods.
findings: Northstar declares currency units, exclusions, opening balances, event timing and a deliberately simple tax rule before reconstruction. Its annual bridges identify movement totals without inventing invoice dates or the debt split.

The balance-sheet, direct and indirect cash-flow, profit and equity calculations retain one company. Corrected June and annual amounts share a revision group; mixing the original interim amount with the revised annual amount is explicitly refused.
The fixed/floating forecast retains one alpha in cash, profit and equity. The text explicitly rejects independently chosen endpoints and supplies x=1-alpha before the later rate comparison.

The portable-state discussion demonstrates why quantity changes, postings, opening state, information cutoff, unknown results and retry identity must agree. It marks implementation and actual fault-testing evidence as pending.

Page 18 begins a distinct parent/subsidiary example with stated ownership, opening books and a supplied narrow tax law. That section remains pending until its full argument has been read. No new defect confirmed in this segment.

equation.exposition_role: Sensitivity derivation and independent arithmetic control.
equation.symbols_units_domain: I(x;r) is annual currency-unit interest, x lies in [0,1], r is an annual dimensionless rate and principal remains 100.
equation.assumptions_timing: The fixed fraction earns 5 percent, floating principal resets for the year, and the same debt allocation is used in all statements.
equation.source_and_equality: Distributing 100(1-x)0.05 yields 5-5x, which added to 100xr gives 5+(100r-5)x exactly.
equation.interpretation: At r=.07 and .09 the interest slopes are 2 and 4; the stipulated 20-percent tax gives cash/profit slopes -1.6 and -3.2.
equation.transition: The prose uses those slopes to distinguish arithmetic validation from mere agreement between authoring frontends.
